questions.prompt: Two threads access the same int, at least one writes, and there is no synchronization. What does the C++ standard say?
options: It is only a problem for floating-point types
It is safe on x86 because int accesses are atomic
The result is one of the two written values
It is a data race: undefined behavior
questions.explanation: Conflicting unsynchronized accesses are a data race, which is undefined behavior regardless of the hardware.

questions.prompt: Two threads each do 500,000 plain increments of a shared int; the program prints 982,415. How many updates were lost? Give an integer.
Which wait is correct for a consumer thread?
questions.explanation: Spurious wake-ups and competing consumers require re-checking the condition with the lock held; the predicate form does that.

questions.prompt: A producer bursts 80 items in 100 ms; the consumer processes 300 items/s. What is the backlog (items) at the end of the burst? Give an integer.
questions.explanation: The consumer removes 300*0.1 = 30 items during the burst: 80-30 = 50.

questions.prompt: Thread 1 locks A then B; thread 2 locks B then A. What can happen and what is the standard fix?
options: Livelock; add a std::this_thread::sleep_for between attempts
Deadlock; lock both with std::scoped_lock (or use a global lock order)
A data race on the mutexes themselves; make the mutexes atomic
Nothing happens, because std::mutex is recursive and re-lockable
questions.explanation: A cycle of waits is a deadlock; scoped_lock acquires several mutexes with a deadlock-avoidance algorithm.

questions.prompt: close() on a blocking queue must call which notification, and why?
options: notify_one on not_empty only, which wakes a single consumer
notify_all, so every blocked producer and consumer re-checks and exits
It must destroy the mutex so the waiting threads are released
None; blocked threads poll the closed flag on their own
questions.explanation: Several threads may be blocked; each must be woken to observe closed_.

questions.prompt: State the locking contract of a bounded producer-consumer queue: what is protected by what, what blocks, what happens on close, and what the queue guarantees about order.
rubric: One mutex protects the container and the closed flag; waits use predicates on condition variables.
push blocks when full, pop blocks when empty and open; close wakes all, push then fails, pop drains then returns nullopt.
FIFO, no item lost or duplicated; no user code runs under the lock.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
